newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong democrats see dollars in postcards.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong democrats see dollars in postcards.

text.p: Hong Kong's Democratic Party is looking to stock up its coffers by selling sets of postcards featuring cartoon drawings of its 19 legislators and party slogans, a local newspaper reported on Saturday.

The party will offer the postcards for sale in the United States and Canada for US$12-13 a set next week, when party leader Martin Lee, whip Szeto Wah and member Andrew Cheng are due to visit, the Hong Kong Standard said.
Two thousand sets of the postcards, illustrated by well-known Hong Kong political cartoonist Zhun Zi, have been printed, it said. They will be sold in Hong Kong in May.

One of the postcards depicts Lee, an outspoken critic of China's plans to disband the elected Legislative Council after it takes back Hong Kong from Britain on July 1, holding the scales of justice underneath the slogan "to oppose all things which are wrong". The party holds the most seats in the current legislature but refused to participate in the Beijing-backed selection of the provisional legislature that will govern Hong Kong after the handover.
